trial_court: Family Court, Rajsamand, S.B. Criminal Revision No. 881 / 2013

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Sagar and Miss. Rani (minor), wife and daughter

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage with respondent No.2 was solemnized about a decade back. Respondents filed a petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C. claiming maintenance allowance. Petitioner disputed the factum of marriage and pleaded that he is not legally wedded wife.

legal_principles.principle: The standard of proof of marriage in summary proceeding under Section 125 Cr.P.C. is not as strict as required in a trial of offence under section 494 of the I.P.C.
legal_principles.held: If the claimant in proceedings under Section 125 of the Code succeeds in showing that she and the respondent have lived together as husband and wife, the Court can presume that they are legally wedded spouses
cited_cases: Dwarika Prasad Satpathy Vs. Bidyut Praya Dixit and Another, (1999) 7 SCC 675

legal_principles.principle: The validity of the marriage for the purpose of summary proceeding under Section 125 Cr.P.C. is to be determined on the basis of the evidence brought on record by the parties.
legal_principles.held: The standard of proof of marriage in such proceeding is not as strict as is required in a trial of offence under section 494 of the I.P.C.
cited_cases: Dwarika Prasad Satpathy Vs. Bidyut Praya Dixit and Another, (1999) 7 SCC 675

outcome.final_order: Maintenance allowance to respondents No.2 & 3 under Section 125 Cr.P.C. was quantified at Rs.5,000 per month, i.e., Rs.2,500 for each of the respondents.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
